jobs.title: Drift Wood #29 · applications
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 19, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. WOOD usually wears oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn even indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers. CHLOE wears enya tee. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Chloe mails four envelopes. Wood mails the back page. Panel 1: a small post office counter, a teenage girl sliding four fat envelopes across, a boy in an overcoat behind her holding a single folded newspaper (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Chloe says "Four. Priority.". Wood says "One. Media rate. It's the back page.". Panel 2: close-up of four thick envelopes stacked on a postal scale, city names visible on the addresses. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teenage boy holding a newspaper open to the comics page toward a girl at a post office counter, hopeful (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Wood says "I'm sending this to my grandmother in Coos Bay. She's my readership.". Chloe says "She's a readership.". Panel 4: two teenagers leaving a small post office in opposite directions under a wet flag hanging still on its pole, black and white, no words (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
